Together, our findings establish chromatin mobility as a regulated property of cell state, with WNT/{beta}-catenin signalling and CDX factors acting as mediators that fine-tune the sampling of 3D chromatin interactions during cell state transitions.

title: Glutathione Protects Hematopoietic Stem Cells from Proteotoxic Stress
authors: Paul, A.; Tom, H.; Merchant, S.; Phan, J.; Lemoff, A.; Mathews, T. P.; Karner, C. M.; Hoxaj, G.; Zhao, Z.; Morrison, S. J.
institution: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
abstract: Glutathione is a redox buffer, best known for preventing oxidative stress and ferroptosis, but rarely studied in stem cells. We studied glutathione function in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) by deleting the glutamate-cysteine ligase catalytic subunit (GCLC), which synthesizes glutathione, or glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), which employs glutathione to prevent ferroptosis. GCLC deficiency eliminated glutathione from hematopoietic cells, severely impairing HSC function and hematopoiesis. In contrast, GPX4 deficiency did not affect HSC function and had little effect on hematopoiesis, even after vitamin E depletion, suggesting glutathione has ferroptosis-independent functions in HSCs. Consistent with this, GCLC deficiency increased reactive oxygen species levels in hematopoietic cells. But treatment with antioxidants or ferroptosis inhibitors gave little or no rescue of HSC function despite reducing ROS levels. Rather, GCLC-deficient, but not GPX4-deficient, HSCs exhibited unfolded protein accumulation, proteostatic stress, and cell death marked by elevated p53 levels and Annexin V staining. Deficiency for p53 prolonged the function of GCLC-deficient HSCs after transplantation. Glutathione is thus necessary in HSCs for proteostasis but may be dispensable for ferroptosis inhibition in vivo.

title: Predicted structure of the complete CPLANE complex reveals novel interactors and mechanisms of Jbts17 during ciliogenesis
authors: Gardner, T. P.; Prolomova, A.; Lee, C.; Marcotte, E. M.; Wallingford, J. B.
institution: The University of Texas at Austin
abstract: Cilia are highly conserved organelles that use hundreds of unique proteins to drive extracellular motility and serve as signaling hubs for eukaryotic cells. The Ciliogenesis and Planar Polarity Effector (CPLANE) protein complex controls basal body docking during early ciliogenesis and recruits the intraflagellar transport (IFT) proteins to the base of growing cilia. Leveraging recent advantages in deep learning neural networks and high-performance computing, we predict the structure of JBTS17, the largest CPLANE subunit, and the tertiary structure of the complete CPLANE complex, revealing direct contacts between JBTS17 and three other CPLANE members. We then used this model for an in silico protein-protein interaction screen that identified several novel JBTS17 interactors. Experiments in Xenopus confirmed a functional link in vivo between Jbts17 and the Spinocerebellar ataxia-associated protein TTBK2. The data provide new insights into mechanisms of CPLANE function during ciliogenesis and demonstrate the power of modeling protein complexes for the discovery of physical and functional protein interactions in cell homeostasis and disease.

title: The single-PDZ domain protein TXBP-3 regulates contractility in the C. elegans spermatheca
authors: Khalid, M.; Cram, E. J.
abstract: In the C. elegans reproductive system, oocyte transit through the spermatheca relies on parallel calcium and Rho-dependent signaling pathways to regulate actomyosin contractility. Here, we identify the conserved single-PDZ domain protein TXBP-3/TAX1BP3 as a dosage-dependent regulator of spermathecal contractility. TXBP-3 is expressed in contractile tissues, including the spermatheca and spermathecal-uterine (sp-ut) valve. Animals lacking txbp-3 do not display overt phenotypes or defects in ovulation. However, in nematodes expressing the genetically encoded calcium sensor GCaMP, deletion of txbp-3 results in more rapid transit of embryos through the spermatheca. Conversely, tissue-specific overexpression of TXBP-3 results in slower transit times due to hypercontraction of the spermathecal neck and sp-ut valve, causing oocyte severing and failures of embryos to exit the spermatheca. We find TXBP-3 promotes the active phosphorylated state of the calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) UNC-43. When TXBP-3 is overexpressed or unc-43 is depleted, ovulations in which the embryo fails to exit show disrupted calcium signaling. Additionally, TXBP-3 functions independently of the RhoGEF RHGF-1 and in parallel with the RhoGAP SPV-1 to maintain the alignment of actin fiber bundles and protect embryo structural integrity. Together, our results establish TXBP-3 as a regulator of contractility, kinase activation, and cytoskeletal architecture in contractile tissues.

title: YY1 phosphorylation links non-apoptotic caspase-8 signaling to MASH fibrosis
authors: Wang, X.; Jung, E. J.; Faccioli, L. A. P.; Stupack, D. G.; Soto-Gutierrez, A.; Tabas, I.
abstract: Background & Aims: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a leading cause of chronic liver disease, and liver fibrosis is the principal determinant of disease progression and clinical outcome. We recently showed that non-apoptotic caspase-8 in hepatocytes is upregulated in MASH and leads to the induction and secretion of meteorin, which promotes hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and liver fibrosis. We address here the major mechanistic question arising from this study, namely how non-apoptotic caspase-8 induces pro-fibrotic meteorin in hepatocytes in MASH. Methods: Mechanistic studies were performed using AML12 hepatocytes; primary mouse and human hepatocytes; and diet-induced mouse models of MASH with hepatocyte-specific caspase-8 deletion. YY1 post-translational modifications were identified by LC-MS/MS and investigated using phosphorylation-defective and phosphomimetic YY1 mutants. Genetic and biochemical approaches were used to interrogate the caspase-8 DED-SRC-GSK3b; pathway, and its relevance was assessed in human MASH liver specimens. Results: In vitro mechanistic studies showed that the amino-terminal death effector domain (DED) of caspase-8 activated a SRC-GSK3b signaling cascade that promoted phosphorylation of YY1 at Ser247, resulting in YY1 nuclear localization and Metrn induction. Disruption of the conserved DED RXDLL motif impaired SRC activation, YY1 phosphorylation, and Metrn expression. Hepatocyte YY1 overexpression increased Metrn expression and fibrosis in wild-type MASH mice but not in hepatocyte-caspase-8-deficient mice. In contrast, phosphomimetic YY1-S247D restored these endpoints even when hepatocyte caspase-8 was lacking. Studies in primary mouse and human hepatocytes and human MASH liver specimens supported conservation of this signaling pathway. Conclusions: These findings identify YY1 Ser247 phosphorylation as a critical molecular event linking non-apoptotic hepatocyte caspase-8 signaling to METRN induction and MASH fibrosis and define a previously unrecognized DED-SRC-GSK3b-YY1 signaling axis with potential therapeutic relevance.

title: The annexin A1 mimetic peptide Ac2-26 promotes inflammation-resolution and stimulates skeletal muscle regeneration in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy
authors: Rehman, H.; Lu, X.; Nasrallah, S. M.; Sharma, B.; Lies, S.; Adhikari, S.; Welc, S. S.; Markworth, J. F.
institution: Department of Animal Sciences, College of Agriculture, Purdue University, West Lafayette, IN, USA.
abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disorder mainly affecting young boys characterized by repeated cycles of myofiber injury/regeneration and chronic muscle inflammation. Although glucocorticoids can slow disease progression, their potential long-term adverse effects highlight the need for new steroid-sparing therapies for DMD. Annexin A1 (ANXA1) is a glucocorticoid-induced pro-resolving protein that signals primarily through formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2). We investigated whether the ANXA1 mimetic peptide Ac2-26 could reduce inflammation, stimulate tissue regeneration, and improve skeletal muscle function in muscular dystrophy. 3-week-old dystrophin-deficient male mdx mice were randomized to receive daily intraperitoneal injections of vehicle control, deflazacort (1 mg/kg/day), or Ac2-26 (1 mg/kg/day) for a duration of 5-weeks. Body composition, skeletal muscle mass, contractile function, and tissue histopathology/immune-cell infiltration were assessed at 8-weeks of age. Direct effects on myogenesis were also examined in vitro using primary D2-mdx myoblasts. ANXA1 was expressed predominantly by myeloid cells rather than resident dystrophic muscle cells. Both deflazacort and Ac2-26 markedly reduced intramuscular inflammation and increased myofiber size. However, Ac2-26 produced broader anabolic and functional benefits, increasing body-weight gain, lean body mass, hindlimb muscle weights, and absolute contractile force. Ac2-26 treatment also directly promoted myogenesis of dystrophic myoblasts in vitro, while pharmacological FPR2 blockade impaired myotube development. Overall, Ac2-26 mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of deflazacort while providing superior benefits for body weight and composition, skeletal muscle growth, myofiber regeneration, and absolute muscle strength. These findings support therapeutic targeting of the ANXA1-FPR2 axis as a potential safe and effective steroid-sparing immunomodulatory strategy for DMD.

title: The protective effect of NGF mutant CHF6467 in SH SY5Y cells exposed to Aβ(1-42): a pharmacometabolomic approach
authors: Napolitano, E.; Marino, C.; Grimaldi, M.; Buonocore, M.; Santoro, A.; Barbato, G.; D'Ursi, A. M.
abstract: Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) supports neuronal survival, plasticity, and growth by binding to p75NTR and TrkA receptors. There is a strong link between NGF and the cholinergic hippocampus, and changes in NGF pathways are observed in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Research shows NGF's neuroprotective and regenerative effects on cholinergic neurons, with positive results in AD models and clinical studies. However, NGF therapy faces challenges: limited blood-brain barrier crossing and dose-dependent pain. To address pain, a mutated NGF called CHF6467 was developed. Thanks to the R100E mutation, it prevents binding to p75NTR while maintaining TrkA affinity, which helps reduce pain side effects. Understanding CHF6467's mechanism remains a challenge. In this context, untargeted metabolomics is effective for uncovering unforeseen responses, making it suitable for assessing CHF6467's overall effects. Building on our previous research and recognizing the importance of amyloid-{beta} peptide as a critical pathological marker of AD, we used NMR-metabolomics to study the effect of CHF6467 on SH-SY5Y cells. The study examined metabolomic profiles of cells treated with CHF6467, with and without A{beta}(1-42), using NMR. Results show CHF6467 influences the metabolic changes caused by A{beta}(1-42), inducing biochemical effects consistent with the promotion of phospholipid precursors, reduced glutamate excitotoxicity, and restored energy metabolism.

title: A two-step organoid screen identifies transient p53 activation as a senolytic strategy for radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction
authors: Soto-Gamez, A.; Wu, Y.; Hageman, E.; Brouwer, U.; Cinat, D.; Vissink, A.; Demaria, M.; Barazzuol, L.; Pringle, S. A.; Coppes, R. P.
abstract: Radiotherapy significantly improves the survival of head and neck cancer patients. However, it frequently damages the salivary glands, causing persistent hyposalivation and xerostomia. Radiation-induced cellular senescence within the salivary gland stem/progenitor cell niche contributes to hyposalivation, suggesting that selective elimination of senescent cells could promote tissue recovery. However, the effectiveness of senolytic compounds is strongly context dependent, varying with tissue of origin and potentially impairing regenerative cells required for functional restoration. Here, we developed a two-step organoid-based screening methodology that integrates the preferential induction of apoptosis in irradiated, senescence enriched, salivary gland organoids with the preservation of stem/progenitor cell regenerative capacity. As a first step, the senolytic activity of candidate drugs was tested to identify drugs that induced apoptosis in senescent cells of irradiated organoids but were not or less toxic to unirradiated organoids. As a second step, the confirmed senolytic compounds were tested for effects on stem cell self-renewal potential. Using this approach, we identified Nutlin3a, an MDM2 inhibitor and p53 activator, as the compound with the most favorable toxicity profile in salivary glands. Last, we confirmed the anti-senescence and pro-regenerative potential of Nutlin3a in an in vivo mouse model of radiation-induced hyposalivation, where localized Nutlin3a delivery resulted in a robust increase in saliva production, as early as two weeks after administration. These findings establish an organoid-based strategy for identifying tissue-adapted senolytic interventions and propose transient local p53 activation with Nutlin3a as a potential approach to mitigate radiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction.

title: DLGAP5 promotes vascular cell proliferation and remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension
authors: Dey, T.; Zhyvylo, I.; Goncharov, D.; Lin, D.; Greenland, J. R.; Wolters, P. J.; Gomez, D.; Jiang, L.; Goncharova, E. A.
institution: University of California Davis School of Medicine
abstract: Background: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) manifests by pulmonary vascular remodeling, caused by hyper-proliferation and apoptosis resistance of resident PA cells, elevated right ventricular (RV) afterload, and death of RV failure. The goal of this study is to determine the role and mechanisms of action of mitotic spindle-associated microtubule regulator DLG associated protein 5 (DLGAP5) in pulmonary vascular remodeling in PAH. Methods: DLGAP5 expression was assessed in human PAH transcriptomic datasets, PAH patients' lung tissues, pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), and pulmonary artery adventitial fibroblasts (PAAFs). Loss-of-function, molecular, functional, RNAseq, and network analyses were performed. Smooth muscle (SM)-specific DLGAP5 knockdown using adeno-associated virus serotype 6 (AAV6) in mice with SU5416/hypoxia-induced PH was performed. Results: DLGAP5 was overaccumulated in small muscular PAs, PASMCs, and PAAFs from PAH lungs. siRNA DLGAP5 down-regulated cyclin A2, suppressed hyper-proliferation, increased pro-apoptotic BIM, and induced apoptosis in human PAH PASMCs and PAAFs. DEP domain containing 1 (DEPDC1) was identified and validated as a downstream effector of DLGAP5 in PAH PASMCs responsible for hyper-proliferation and apoptosis resistance of human PAH PASMCs. SM-specific DLGAP5 knockdown with AAV6-enTagln-shDLGAP5 reversed DEPDC1 overaccumulation in small muscular PAs, reduced PA medial thickness, RV systolic pressure, mean PA pressure, and RV hypertrophy in mice with SuHx-induced PH. Conclusions: DLGAP5 supports proliferation and survival of human PAH PASMCs and PAAFs through up-regulation of cyclin A2, DEPDC1, and suppression of BIM, and promotes PA remodeling and PH in mice. DLGAP5 could serve as a potential molecular target to attenuate pulmonary vascular remodeling in PAH.

title: Dynamic membrane organization coordinates protein-O-mannosylation and proteostasis in mycobacteria.
authors: Riviere, M.; Riviere, C.; Publicola, G.; Stella, A.; Burlet-Schlitz, O.; Nigou, J.
abstract: Integral membrane enzymes operate within molecular environments, yet how these are organized remains poorly understood. Using M. smegmatis as a mycobacterial model, we define the membrane environment of the protein O-mannosyltransferase MtPMT through stratified interactomics combining affinity purification-mass spectrometry under four stringencies with a persistence score. This approach resolves a persistent membrane-associated core of 108 proteins from more transient layers, revealing a hierarchically organized landscape enriched in Sec protein translocation, protein biogenesis and envelope proteostasis machineries. Reciprocal affinity purification and in vivo FRET identify YajC and FtsH as neighbors of MtPMT, while structural modelling supports integration within a Sec-associated assembly. Genetic disruption of factors reduces O-mannosylation activity, demonstrating dependence on platform integrity. The MtPMT-associated network is remodelled during growth, indicating an adaptive system. Loss of POM compromises envelope permeability and stress resilience, linking O-mannosylation to fitness. Together, our results establish protein O-mannosylation as an integrated component of a dynamic membrane platform coordinating secretion, membrane protein biogenesis and proteostasis. Our findings support a model in which mycobacterial membranes contain specialized domains dynamically modulated by physiological state.

title: Fast single molecule localization microscopy in 3D
authors: Allgeyer, E.; Richens, J. H.; Lefevere-Laoide, J.; Paluch, E. K.; Sirinakis, G.; St Johnston, D.
abstract: Super-resolution methods, such as single molecule localisation microscopy (SMLM), can determine the distribution of specific proteins at the nanometre scale. However, three-dimensional (3D) SMLM is typically limited to thin sections and requires prohibitively long acquisition times to image complete cells. Here we introduce a 3D SMLM imaging modality, Intrinsic3D, that combines the speed and optical sectioning of oblique plane microscopy (OPM) with the nanometre resolution of SMLM to determine the position of single molecule emitters throughout complete volumes more than an order-of-magnitude faster over regular DNA-PAINT. By scanning the oblique light sheet across the volume and combining localization information from two or more adjacent planes, an emitter's x, y and z position is determined, eliminating the need for post-processing steps to stitch multiple image stacks together. We demonstrate resolution and speed by imaging nuclear pore complexes in U2OS cells and Drosophila egg chambers. As a proof-of-concept, we map the 3D distribution of the cell-adhesion protein DE-cadherin in the Drosophila follicular epithelium and show that spot adherens junctions are enriched near tricellular junctions and contain more E-cadherin than the apical adherens junctions, suggesting that spot junctions play a wider role in cell-cell adhesion than previously appreciated. Finally, we examine the organization of Gliotactin, a tricellular septate junction protein relative to E-cadherin using exchange-PAINT. These investigations demonstrate that Intrinsic3D delivers rapid 3D protein mapping in whole cells. Combining Intrinsic3D with existing multiplex and resolution enhancing methods (e.g. exchange-PAINT and RESI) will enable multicolour, 3D in situ spatial proteomics in tissue samples and bridge the gap between SMLM and systems-level cell biology.

title: AI-assisted quantification of the clonogenic assay
authors: Radstake, W. E.; Kneringer, A.; Denbeigh, J. M.; Rangan, K.; Bhalloo, M.; Beltran, C. J.
institution: Department of Radiation Oncology, Mayo Clinic, Jacksonville, United States
abstract: The clonogenic assay is the foundational standard for evaluating cellular radiosensitivity, yet its manual quantification is limited by labor-intensive processing, high inter-observer variability, and a reductive binary scoring system. Here, we present and validate a deep learning-based segmentation pipeline for the automated, high-throughput quantification of mammalian cell survival across diverse radiation qualities (photons, protons, and carbon ions). By benchmarking against expert consensus using Bland-Altman analysis, we demonstrate that this AI framework consistently operates within natural human error margins. Crucially, transitioning to automated whole-well image-based analysis enables the extraction of continuous multidimensional data, including colony area, density, and cellularity. This phenotypic profiling successfully identified and quantified high-cellularity colonies formed by radioresistant BxPC-3 cells under particle irradiation. Coupled with rapid image acquisition platforms, this methodology significantly reduces processing bottlenecks while standardizing the derivation of relative biological effectiveness (RBE). By advancing beyond binary survival metrics to continuous morphological profiling, this framework provides a vital new analytical dimension for investigating structural mechanisms of radioresistance.
